overview: Brick-built display-scale (roughly 12–16 bricks tall) figure inspired by the reference: a blond-haired hero in a white outfit holding a blue lightsaber. Build as a simple, sturdy “chibi statue” with a compact internal core and chunky limbs so it’s stable and achievable with the available plates/bricks and clear/trans-blue elements.

subassemblies.name: Feet + Lower Legs
subassemblies.description: Two blocky feet and short shins to match the white boots/pants in the reference. Use mostly white bricks/plates (3004/3005/3024/3023) with a few tan/light-brown accents near the lower leg to hint at the printed leg detail. Connect to hips with a 2-stud-wide stance for stability.

subassemblies.name: Hips/Pelvis
subassemblies.description: A compact 4x4-ish core section in white with a thin dark-red/brown band around the front to suggest the belt. This is the main structural anchor tying both legs to the torso.

subassemblies.name: Torso/Chest
subassemblies.description: White outer shell around a small internal core (light bluish gray/dark bluish gray) to keep it rigid. Add a subtle V/diagonal ‘robe’ line using dark pieces or thin plate layering on the front. Keep sides mostly smooth and boxy.

subassemblies.name: Arms (Both)
subassemblies.description: Two short, chunky arms in white, angled forward so the hands meet at center. Build each as a 1–2 stud thick assembly; use hinge/clip-style connections if available in your lot, otherwise use stepped plates to create the forward pose.

subassemblies.name: Hands/Grip Block
subassemblies.description: A small central grip block in tan/light nougat tones to represent minifig hands, designed to clamp the saber hilt between both arms. Prioritize strength: lock it into the torso with plates so the saber can’t wobble.

subassemblies.name: Lightsaber Hilt
subassemblies.description: Cylindrical-looking gray/silver stack using light/dark bluish gray and flat silver elements (e.g., 6141/18976/4528 where workable) in a short handle. Attach firmly into the grip block.

subassemblies.name: Lightsaber Blade
subassemblies.description: A straight blue/transparent-blue blade using trans-clear/trans-blue look: stack trans-clear elements and/or use clear pieces backed by medium/dark azure plates to read as a glowing blade. Keep it one-stud wide and reinforce at the base.

subassemblies.name: Neck + Head
subassemblies.description: A 3x3-ish tan/medium-nougat ‘head’ block with a simple face suggestion (dark tiles/plates for eyes/brows). Mount on a short neck so the head sits slightly forward like the reference.

subassemblies.name: Hair
subassemblies.description: Layered blond ‘hair’ cap using tan/yellow plates (tan, yellow, bright light yellow) in stepped layers to imitate swept hair. Slight overhang on the forehead/sides for silhouette.

subassemblies.name: Back Bracing (Optional)
subassemblies.description: Hidden reinforcement on the back of torso and hips (light bluish gray/dark bluish gray) to prevent the forward-posed arms/saber from tipping the model. Can also widen the back footprint subtly.

notes: Color matching can be approximate: use white as the dominant outfit color; add a dark-red/brown belt stripe at the waist; use tan/yellow for hair.
Prioritize a strong internal core running from feet through hips into torso; the saber/arms add forward leverage.
Keep the blade either mostly trans-clear with blue backing accents, or a mix of medium/dark azure plates if you don’t have enough clear pieces for length.
If you lack true hinges/clips for arm posing, use stepped plate offsets to angle the forearms inward toward the hilt.
